newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Iran signs pact to build Philippine oil refinery.
newsitem.headline: Iran signs pact to build Philippine oil refinery.

text.p: Members of an Iranian government mission signed a memorandum of agreement on Friday to pursue oil-related and cement ventures with Filipino investors.
A statement from the presidential palace said the ventures include the construction of a 150,000 barrel-a-day refinery in Mindanao, southern Philippines, which will start this September.
Liquefied petroleum depots will also be put up in Mindanao.
A cement plant, a rolling steel mill and an assembly plant for farm tractors, engines and trucks will be built.
President Fidel Ramos witnessed the signing during a courtesy call of a technical mission led by the secretary-general of the Iran Chamber of Commerce, Mines and Industry.
The statement did not state which firms were undertaking the projects.

But it said that signatories to the agreement included officials of Pacific Eastern Petroleum, Minsupala Fastrack Development Corp and Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (ARMM) governor Nur Misuari.
